name: exception-uncaught-build-failure
capturedFrom: probe/bloc_probe on device A015 (Android 16, Flutter 3.44.1), 2026-08-26. 29-second window (16s watched plus the DDS backlog delivered on subscribe), covering three workload cycles. The probe's `crash` phase arms a widget that throws inside `build`, so the framework reports it through `FlutterError.reportError` and the inspector posts a `Flutter.Error` event.
why:
The right answer is `exception`, and the engine should commit to it.

Two `Flutter.Error` events carry an uncaught `Bad state: bloc_probe: deliberate uncaught build failure`, each with a full stack whose first frame is `_CrashCell.build.<anonymous closure> (package:bloc_probe/main.dart:218:13)`. That is a definite defect rather than a slow patch of frames: the throw escaped application code, the framework abandoned that subtree, and it substituted an ErrorWidget. A screen failed to render.

Jank is the only competing explanation and it must lose, for a reason visible in the events rather than in the priority ordering. 49 of 202 frames (24.3%) missed budget, which on its own clears the jank hypothesis' 20% bar — but the worst frame of the session, frm_00062 at 274.68ms with 186.94ms of build against 6.65ms of raster, is the event immediately after exc_00061. The jank hypothesis' own anchor is downstream of the exception: reporting a structured error and rebuilding the failed subtree as an ErrorWidget is what made that frame the worst one. Treating the symptom as the cause would send a reader to the frame budget when a widget is throwing. The rest of the jank is the probe's designed workload — 60 BlocBuilders rebuilding per transition — not a fault.

Nothing else competes: zero network events, and all 87 log lines are severity info.

Confidence in the low 0.8s is right. There is a hard artefact with a stack trace, which is more than the jank pair ever gets, but nothing corroborates *why* the widget threw — no failing request before it, no error or warning log near it. Committed, not certain.

The anchor must be cited. An exception verdict that does not hand back the event id of the exception it rests on cannot be checked by the person reading it, and the id is what makes `get_exceptions` reproduce the same stack.

One thing this incident deliberately does not assert: the route. The diagnosis attributes the anchor to `/detail`, because ordering is by receipt time and the structured error arrives asynchronously — it can land after the navigation event for a push that happened later in the app. Route attribution is not what this golden measures, so it is not in `expect`.

findings.claim: 5027 widget rebuild(s) across 46 frame(s). Busiest: unknown — 5012 rebuild(s) over 226 frame(s). No hotspot resolved to your own code.
findings.fix: Narrow the rebuild scope around unknown. Split the widget so only the part that depends on changing state rebuilds, add const constructors, and move computation out of build().

findings.claim: Janky frames spend most of their time building: mean build 31.18ms vs raster 10.07ms.
findings.fix: Build-phase heavy: move expensive work out of build(), use const widgets, cache computed values, and narrow the rebuild scope with smaller widgets or selectors.

findings.claim: 46 of 49 janky frames (94%) fell within 1000ms of provider state activity (1301 events). For comparison, 59% of the 153 smooth frames were also inside a window.
findings.fix: Correlation only, and the window is symmetric, so this does not show the state change came first. limitations: No CPU sampling. A slow build can be attributed to a widget, but not to a specific function — use the DevTools CPU profiler for that.
GC events are not observable: the VM timeline is fetched on demand and not stored, so garbage-collection pauses cannot be ruled in or out.
Frames are only captured while connected, and older ones roll out of the retention window.
State changes are counted, never read: neither Riverpod nor Provider exposes values or provider names through the VM Service, so no claim is made about which provider is responsible.
Rebuild totals cover the busiest locations in each frame, not every rebuild — the long tail is counted but not itemised.
App-versus-package attribution is a path heuristic: getPubRootDirectories is empty until a DevTools client sets it, so there is no authoritative project root.

notes: 6 frame(s) rebuilt more locations than are retained; totals cover the busiest locations per frame, not every rebuild.
